context:
Treat responsive behavior as a shared product contract instead of page-local
CSS cleanup. Start by enumerating surfaces, then implement the smallest
shared primitives and route overrides needed to satisfy the PR #246 evidence.
Prefer tests that catch overflow and hidden navigation before relying on
manual screenshots alone.
description:
PR #246 found that the Results Explorer has cross-route responsive risks:
Query disappears from the 390px secondary nav, dense tables clip columns and
row actions, and chart/table affordances are inconsistent at mobile and
tablet widths. These are not isolated CSS defects; they are route-level
responsive contracts that must be specified, implemented, and regression
tested.

This TODO creates the integrated responsive remediation plan for the PR #246
evidence. It should be worked alongside page-specific retheme items, but it
owns the shared rules for navigation, horizontal scroll affordances, sticky
first/action columns, card fallbacks, focus-visible semantics, and target
reachability.

anti_patterns.dont: accept horizontal scrolling without a visible affordance or sticky context.
fix one route by adding bespoke responsive behavior that contradicts another route.
hide route navigation on mobile without an obvious menu, wrap, or scroll cue.
make mobile users reach row actions only by discovering invisible horizontal overflow.
use a focus ring to represent selected rows or active chart data.

preserves.behavior: All public Results Explorer routes and share URLs.
Dense desktop data scanning at 1280px and 1600px.
High-contrast/reduced-color behavior for heatmaps and charts.
Keyboard access to nav, filter controls, table sort, chart tabs, compare selection, disclosures, and row actions.

verifications.command: cd results-explorer && npm test -- src/components/__tests__ src/pages/__tests__
verifications.expected: all relevant unit and accessibility tests pass

verifications.command: cd results-explorer && npm run test:e2e:fixtures && npm run build && npx playwright test --project=chromium --grep "responsive|layout|a11y|mobile"
verifications.expected: responsive browser smoke passes or skipped grep is documented

verifications.command: echo 'Manual: recapture audited routes at 390 and 768 and compare against PR #246 mobile/tablet screenshots'
verifications.description: Manual mobile/tablet PR #246 evidence recapture is clean
verifications.expected: no hidden nav item, clipped row action, or chart/table overflow remains without affordance

work_units.summary: Write explicit responsive contracts for every audited route

work_units.notes:
Fix the 390px nav state where `Query` is off-canvas with no strong menu
or scroll cue. The active route should remain discoverable on mobile,
including when the user is already on `/results/query`. Use a wrapped nav,
mobile menu, or visible horizontal-scroll affordance with scroll shadow.

Verify target sizes are practical for touch and that keyboard focus order
through nav items is predictable.
work_units.summary: Make mobile secondary navigation fully discoverable
Harden shared table overflow affordances and action reachability

work_units.notes:
Fix chart containers so SVGs never exceed their cards at 390px or 768px.
Include Result Detail and Compare first because PR #246 captured concrete
clipping and sparse plot evidence. Add guardrails for clipped labels,
legends overlapping plot content, huge empty plot regions, and delayed
ResizeObserver sizing.

Normalize focus-visible, active, selected, hover, disabled, and warning states
Add viewport regression checks for responsive contracts
